newsitem.title: FINLAND: CARNEGIE TO BUY ERIK SELIN OPS, BROKERAGES SAY.
newsitem.headline: CARNEGIE TO BUY ERIK SELIN OPS, BROKERAGES SAY.

text.p: The brokerage, asset management and mutual fund operations of Carnegie and Pankkiiriliike Erik Selin Ab Bankirfirma will be merged by June 15, the companies said in a joint statement on Friday.

The merger will be implemented through a purchase by Carnegie of Erik Selin's business operations including the mutual funds arm Erik Selin Rahasto Oy, they said, adding the deal did not cover other operations of the Selin Finance group.
The price of the deal was not given.

The new entity would employ slightly over 50 people. The two companies' combined market share in brokering is about 10 percent. Their asset management operations and mutual funds look after total capital of slightly more than two billion markka.

Matti Kinnunen, chairman of the board of Carnegie Securities Finland, said in the statement that the merger aimed to turn Carnegie into a leading investment services company independent of banks. By joining forces with Selin, Carnegie would reach a similar leading position in Finland as it already has in other Nordic countries, he said.
In a separate statement, Carnegie said its managing director Magnus von Knorring had decided to leave the company.
Kinnunen would become managing director during a transition period while Carnegie's new expanded brokerage operations would be restructured into a branch of the Swedish parent company D. Carnegie AB.
The new Carnegie-Selin entity's asset management and mutual funds operations would not be included in the new branch restructuring, Carnegie said.
Carnegie is 55-percent owned by British investment bank and fund management group Singer&Friedlander and 45-percent by Carnegie staff, it said.
